title: The Strategic Case for Hybrid AC-DC Power
gist: AI-driven power demand is turning the long-tolerated inefficiency of AC-to-DC conversion into a material cost, pushing data centers, industrial plants, and commercial buildings toward hybrid AC-DC architectures; BCG and ABB argue the next two to three years of capital and spec decisions will set the standards that govern the next decade.

themes.theme: AC-DC mismatch and the AI trigger

insights.claim: Solar PV generation, battery storage, data centers, and EVs are all natively DC loads and sources, but the distribution grid connecting them still runs on AC architecture dating to the 1890s, creating a structural mismatch between how energy is produced/consumed and how it is delivered.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Every new DC-native load (AI data centers, EV fleets, battery storage) added to an AC grid adds conversion losses and capex that a redesigned hybrid architecture could avoid.
insights.quote: The dominant new energy sources and loads are natively direct current (DC): solar PV generates it, batteries store it, and data centers and EVs consume it. Yet the distribution infrastructure connecting them still runs on alternating current (AC), the architecture that has prevailed since the 1890s.
insights.locator: The world's energy system is quietly rewiring itself.

insights.claim: AC-to-DC conversion losses were historically an acceptable inefficiency, but the scaling of AI computing to gigawatt-scale hyperscale campuses is magnifying the cost of unnecessary conversion stages, making the inefficiency material rather than negligible.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: AI compute demand is the forcing function that makes hybrid AC-DC economically urgent now, after decades where it wasn't worth solving.
insights.quote: The rapid scaling of AI computing power (known familiarly as AI compute) is changing that calculus. To keep up with demand, hyperscale campuses will need to operate at gigawatt scale, magnifying the cost of unnecessary conversions.
insights.locator: That mismatch was once an acceptable inefficiency.

insights.claim: Current AI data center infrastructure routes every watt of power through multiple AC-DC conversion stages before it reaches a server, not because those stages are technically necessary but because the underlying infrastructure predates the AI-era loads it now serves.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Legacy AC infrastructure is effectively a hidden efficiency tax on AI compute economics; operators who cut conversion stages can turn saved energy directly into usable compute or revenue.
insights.quote: These facilities force every watt through multiple conversion stages before it reaches a server—stages that exist not because they are necessary but because the infrastructure predates the loads it now serves.
insights.locator: That mismatch was once an acceptable inefficiency.

insights.claim: The likely end-state of the power system transition is not a fully DC grid but a hybrid model: AC remains the backbone for most transmission and regional distribution, while DC takes over high-density, behind-the-meter applications across data centers, industrial plants, commercial buildings, and residential buildings.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Investors and operators should model incremental hybrid retrofits (behind-the-meter DC backbones) rather than betting on wholesale grid replacement.
insights.quote: The destination is not an all-DC grid, but a hybrid architecture: AC remains the backbone of most transmission and regional distribution, while DC increasingly powers high-density applications, mostly behind the meter.
insights.locator: In four sectors—data centers, industrial plants, commercial buildings, and residential buildings

insights.claim: For AI data centers, DC is rapidly becoming the required (not merely optional) architecture because it meets the power density demands of next-generation AI hardware, fits more compute behind a scarce grid connection, and converts efficiency gains directly into revenue.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Hyperscalers and data center equipment vendors should treat DC-native power design as a near-term requirement, not a future option; grid-connection scarcity makes conversion efficiency a direct revenue lever.
insights.quote: For AI data centers, DC is rapidly becoming the required architecture. It meets the power density demands of next-generation AI hardware, fits more compute behind a scarce grid connection, and turns efficiency gains directly into revenue.
insights.locator: A paper published by BCG in collaboration with ABB

insights.claim: For automation-intensive industrial plants, the business case for hybrid AC-DC architecture is positive from day one of operation because most factories already contain DC-native loads, unlike other sectors where the case still depends on future conditions.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Industrial plant operators have the clearest, fastest payback case for hybrid retrofits among the four sectors studied, making them a near-term adoption segment to watch.
insights.quote: For automation-intensive industrial plants, the business case for hybrid architecture is positive from the first day of operation, driven by the DC-native loads that most factories already contain.
insights.locator: A paper published by BCG in collaboration with ABB

insights.claim: For large commercial buildings, DC pays off selectively: it creates a backbone for major loads such as elevators, climate-control systems, and energy storage, while tenant-facing systems remain on AC, implying a partial rather than building-wide conversion strategy is optimal.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Commercial building owners can capture DC efficiency gains on core infrastructure loads without needing to convert tenant-facing electrical systems, lowering the capital bar for adoption.
insights.quote: For large commercial buildings, DC pays off by creating a backbone for major loads such as elevators, climate-control systems, and energy storage while leaving tenant-facing systems on AC.
insights.locator: A paper published by BCG in collaboration with ABB

insights.claim: For residential buildings, the business case for hybrid AC-DC architecture is not yet compelling today, but policy shifts already on the calendar could improve the economics and shift the timing of adoption.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Residential DC adoption is a policy-contingent, later-stage opportunity; watch for regulatory or incentive changes as the catalyst that would move this segment from uneconomic to viable.
insights.quote: For residential buildings, the business case for hybrid architecture is not yet compelling, but policy shifts on the calendar may improve the economics.
insights.locator: A paper published by BCG in collaboration with ABB

insights.claim: The barriers slowing hybrid AC-DC adoption are systemic and organizational rather than technical, meaning the transition is fundamentally a coordination problem among suppliers, operators, and developers rather than an unsolved engineering challenge.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Because the constraint is coordination, not technology, the winners will be organizations that move first on specifications and standards, not necessarily those with the best engineering.
insights.quote: The barriers to faster adoption are systemic rather than technical, which means that this is more of a coordination problem than an engineering issue.
insights.locator: The barriers to faster adoption are systemic rather than technical

insights.claim: Equipment and automation suppliers, hyperscalers, industrial operators, and large developers that commit capital and set specifications over the next two to three years will shape the hybrid AC-DC transition's cost curves, voltage defaults, and standards for the next decade, rather than simply inheriting rules set by others.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: There is a narrow 2-3 year first-mover window; companies that commit capital and specs now can shape industry-wide voltage standards to their advantage, while late movers become price- and standard-takers.
insights.quote: Equipment and automation suppliers, hyperscalers, industrial operators, and large developers that commit capital and set specifications over the next two to three years will shape the transition rather than inherit it.
insights.locator: The barriers to faster adoption are systemic rather than technical

insights.claim: BCG frames the strategic choice facing every organization in this space as binary: help set the emerging AC-DC standards now, or accept the standards others develop later.
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: Frame near-term electrification capex decisions as a standard-setting race, not just an efficiency upgrade; early movers gain influence over industry-wide specifications.
insights.quote: The question that each organization must answer is whether it will help set the standards or merely accept them as developed by others.
insights.locator: The barriers to faster adoption are systemic rather than technical

insights.claim: The hybrid AC-DC economics referenced in the article come from a study BCG published in collaboration with ABB, a global electrification and automation company with roughly 110,000 employees, listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (ABBN) and Nasdaq Stockholm (ABB).
insights.speaker: https://www.bcg.com/about/people/experts/emmanuel-sissimatos
insights.so_what: ABB is both the research co-sponsor and a direct commercial beneficiary of accelerating hybrid AC-DC infrastructure spend, making its electrification/automation segment a natural proxy for this trend.
insights.quote: ABB is a global technology leader in electrification and automation, enabling a more sustainable and resource-efficient future.
